claim_001.label: SUPPORTED
claim_001.text: Rich handles tuple arguments from __rich_repr__ in a dedicated branch by unpacking the key and child, recursively traversing the child, and assigning the key representation and equals separator to the resulting node.

evidence.note: The frozen source restores a dedicated tuple branch that unpacks key and child, traverses the child, sets key_repr and key_separator, and appends the child node.

claim_001.rationale: The behavior is directly visible in the frozen source at rich/pretty.py lines 681 through 687.

claim_002.label: SUPPORTED
claim_002.text: Rich handles non-tuple arguments from __rich_repr__ as positional values by recursively traversing the argument itself and appending the resulting child node without assigning a key representation.

evidence.note: The frozen source restores a separate else branch that traverses arg directly and appends the resulting node without setting key_repr.
The retained tests document positional rich-repr values and confirm that a tuple value associated with a None key is rendered without a displayed key.

claim_002.rationale: The frozen implementation directly separates non-tuple positional values from keyed tuple arguments, while the retained tests document the expected positional rendering behavior.

claim_003.label: UNSUPPORTED
claim_003.text: The revert was primarily introduced to improve the performance of Rich pretty-print traversal.
claim_003.rationale: The frozen diff and commit history describe reverting None-related pretty handling and do not identify performance as the objective.

claim_004.label: UNSUPPORTED
